what: Fig 5b, bioluminescence images of tumour-bearing mice (rows D0, D7, D14; columns PBS, aPD-L1, BPQDs+NIR, BBPQDs+NIR, BBPQDs+NIR+aPD-L1). Four pairs of panels show the same photograph of four mice (same poses, limbs and tail shapes) under a different colour signal: (A) D0 aPD-L1 and D14 aPD-L1; (B) D0 BPQDs+NIR and D14 BPQDs+NIR; (C) D7 BPQDs+NIR and D0 BBPQDs+NIR; (D) D7 BBPQDs+NIR and D0 BBPQDs+NIR+aPD-L1.
why: Caption: 'Typical in vivo bioluminescence images of tumor burdens on day 0, day 7 and day 14.' Methods: 'the tumor-bearing mice were randomly divided into five groups (n = 6 per group): PBS as the control group; aPD-L1, BPQDs with NIR irradiation; BBPQDs with NIR irradiation; and BBPQDs with NIR irradiation and aPD-L1.' Each panel is therefore a separate imaging session: pairs A and B are the same group imaged 14 days apart, and anaesthetised mice put back in the imager two weeks later do not land in identical poses with identical tail curves; pairs C and D are different treatment groups (different animals) on different days. Source: row and column labels, caption, Methods.
